snippet.title: The Day the Internet Almost Died
snippet.description:

In the late 90s, the Dot-Com Bubble saw investors pour billions into anything ending in .com—from Pets.com to Webvan—no business model required. This $5 TRILLION financial delusion brought the Nasdaq to its knees and wiped out thousands of startups.

We break down the hype-fueled madness, the brutal crash of March 2000, and how a few quiet builders, like Jeff Bezos, ignored the chaos to lay the foundation for the tech giants of the 21st century. The internet didn't die—it rebooted.

snippet.title: The Rise of Paypal Explained Like You're 5
snippet.description:

Across town, two Stanford dropouts are beaming cash between PalmPilots.
Their brutal turf war—complete with coups, fistfights, and exploding servers—will morph into PayPal… and mint the most feared “mafia” in tech history.

In this video, we peel back the duct tape to show how caffeine-fueled chaos, fraud-fighting A.I., and one very ill-timed South-African vacation rewired global finance—and why the shockwaves still power everything from Tesla to LinkedIn.

snippet.title: The Great Depression Explained Like You’re 5
snippet.description:
It's the 1920s. The party's roaring, the stock market is soaring, and everyone from the barber to the shoeshine boy is getting rich. They call it the Roaring Twenties, and people believe the good times will last forever.

But what happens when the music stops?

In this video, we pull back the curtain on the Great Depression, the terrifying economic collapse that wiped out fortunes overnight. We'll explore how reckless speculation, bank failures, and a decade of denial turned the American Dream into a nightmare of hunger and dust.

Discover the chain of events that led to the 1929 stock market crash, the desperate measures of the Hoover administration, and the radical changes of Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal.

Timestamps

🌏 Get exclusive NordVPN deal here ➵  https://NordVPN.com/crayoncapital It’s risk free with Nord’s 30 day money-back guarantee!✌

August 9, 1965. A man sits before a television camera and weeps. His country has just been expelled, left to rot on a swampy island with no water, no resources, and no hope.

Fifty years later, that same island is the richest patch of land on the planet.

This is the true story of Lee Kuan Yew and the rise of Singapore. From a "poisonous shrimp" defense strategy to a ruthless obsession with efficiency, Singapore wasn't just a nation... it was a corporate startup disguised as a country. Fueled by "Asian values," zero-tolerance laws, and a total refusal to fail.

In this video, we explore how a tiny fishing village ignored every rule of economics to go from Third World to First in a single generation.
